description: Our team of 6 NUST students is targeting the Flame in Freefall challenge for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Flame in Freefall is an AI-powered microgravity combustion safety dashboard developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed for spacecraft and lunar/Martian habitats, our solution processes NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets—including Saffire and BASS telemetry—to provide real-time combustion analytics, flame spread rates and spherical diffusion monitoring. By integrating automated OpenCV computer vision pipelines and a Streamlit interactive interface, our dashboard equips astronauts and mission controllers with critical fire safety insights under microgravity conditions.
details:
What it does / How it works: Our Streamlit web dashboard processes NASA microgravity combustion datasets (PSI-100 Saffire-III, BASS, and FLEX) using Python, Pandas, and OpenCV. It extracts flame boundaries via HSV color thresholding, tracks spread rates, and displays real-time telemetry panels.

Benefits & Impact: Fire safety in microgravity (spacecraft, Orion, Lunar Gateway) is uniquely hazardous due to buoyancy absence and high oxygen concentrations. This tool gives real-time diagnostic insights to prevent catastrophic failures.

Tools & Technologies: Python, Streamlit, OpenCV, Pandas, Boto3 (AWS S3 NASA PSI bucket integration), Git/GitHub.
dataRefs: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) - Saffire / BASS Datasets
